name: Soren Westermann
current_role: Co-owner of WS Audiology (via Westermann family); long-time Widex A/S director and engineer
profile: Søren Erik Westermann is a member of the Westermann family that co-founded Danish hearing-aid maker Widex in 1956 (Erik Westermann with Christian Tøpholm). A DTU-trained engineer and long-serving Widex board member, he shares in the family stake in WS Audiology, formed when Widex merged with Sivantos in 2019 and still owned by the Tøpholm and Westermann families alongside EQT.
interesting_fact: Widex's 2019 merger with Siemens' former hearing-aid unit Sivantos created WS Audiology, one of the world's three largest hearing-aid companies, still privately owned by the two founding families plus EQT.
deep_cut_fact: He is a hands-on inventor: with Morten Kroman he is named on US patent 6,658,122 (granted 2003, Widex) for measuring sound at the eardrum in situ via an in-canal microphone and adjusting the hearing aid's signal processing accordingly.
notes: Very private; no personal media presence. Press email is WSA corporate comms from a 2021 release and may be outdated. Relative Adam Westermann (grandson of co-founder) is WSA board vice-chair; family holding is T&W Medical. Alive status not confirmed (patent filings into the 2010s, no death reports found).

name: Wang Shirui
current_role: Founder & CEO, Medlinker (医联) Group; CEO of Future Doctor (未来医生) group
profile: Wang Shirui (王仕锐) founded Chengdu-based Medlinker in 2014 as a professional network for Chinese doctors, growing it into a unicorn backed by Tencent, Sequoia China and China Renaissance focused on internet hospitals and chronic-disease management. He also ran Tencent Trusted Doctors (later Future Doctor, merged into Medlinker) and now pushes the medical LLM MedGPT.
interesting_fact: Medlinker's MedGPT was billed as China's first medical large model approved to give diagnosis and treatment suggestions; Wang says most revenue comes from B2B clients for now.
deep_cut_fact: Before becoming a tech founder he trained as a dentist: he completed the 8-year combined bachelor/master/doctorate program at Sichuan University's West China School of Stomatology and was a research scholar at Harvard.
notes: Twice named to Fortune China 40 Under 40 (2016, 2018). Active in AI-in-medicine discussions (e.g. dialogue with Kevin Kelly). Chinese-language outreach via media@ is likely the best route.

name: Daniel Hager
current_role: Chairman of the Supervisory Board, Hager Group (Hager SE); President of ZVEI (German Electro & Digital Industry Association) since May 2026
profile: Third-generation family owner of Hager Group, the Franco-German maker of electrical installation, energy-distribution and building-automation products (brands Hager, Berker, E3/DC; 13,000+ staff). He joined in 2003, was CEO from 2008 to Nov 2023, then became supervisory board chairman; in May 2026 he was elected ZVEI president with energy transition as a priority.
interesting_fact: Hager sees the firm as straddling two cultures: 'We are perceived as a French company in France and as a German company in Germany' — and sums up its strategy as 'The future is electric.'
deep_cut_fact: Before joining the family business in 2003 he worked outside it: first as a project manager at Eaton Electric, then at wind-farm developer Plambeck Neue Energien — an early renewables stint fitting today's E3/DC home-storage business.
notes: Strong fit for an energy podcast (electrification, home batteries via E3/DC, ZVEI energy-transition agenda). Studied economics in Brussels and Paris. Press contacts listed on May 2026 Hager release.

name: Sir Roger
current_role: Chair, Creative Folkestone; founder of the Roger De Haan Charitable Trust (former Saga chairman)
profile: Sir Roger De Haan (born 1948, Northampton) took over over-50s travel and insurance group Saga from his father Sidney in 1984 and ran it with brother Peter for some 20 years before selling it in a £1.35bn buyout in 2004. Since then he has focused on regenerating Folkestone, buying its harbour and funding arts charity Creative Folkestone and local education. Knighted 2014.
interesting_fact: In 2004, the same year he sold Saga, he bought Folkestone Harbour for £11m; his trust has put about £50m into acquiring and restoring nearly 90 buildings in the town's Creative Quarter.
deep_cut_fact: While running Saga he extended the brand into broadcasting, launching Saga-branded radio stations for older listeners alongside its holidays and financial services.
notes: Input name is truncated: this is Sir Roger De Haan (shared listing with brother Peter De Haan). Low media profile; best route is via his charitable trust's contact form or Creative Folkestone. Avoid political-donation topics.

name: Lance Gokongwei
current_role: President & CEO, JG Summit Holdings (also chairs key affiliates such as Cebu Pacific, Robinsons Land and Universal Robina)
profile: Only son of the late John Gokongwei Jr., Lance Gokongwei runs JG Summit, a Philippine conglomerate spanning Cebu Pacific airline, snack maker Universal Robina, Robinsons property and retail, banking, petrochemicals and stakes in power and telecom. A Penn graduate (finance and applied science, 1988), he is shifting the group from owner-operator to an active investor model.
interesting_fact: Cebu Pacific, the family's budget airline, has been in talks for an order of up to 150 new aircraft, among the largest in Philippine aviation history.
deep_cut_fact: His first job was management trainee at Universal Robina selling Jack 'n Jill snacks door to door to supermarkets and sari-sari stores, paid P2,000 a month and driving an old Datsun with a broken air-conditioner, as he told PLV graduates in 2019.
notes: Low-key, rarely gives interviews; corporate route via JG Summit IR/corporate communications. Group has power and data-related interests relevant to energy podcast.

name: Liselott Tham
current_role: Private investor; second-largest shareholder of H&M (approx. 5% stake)
profile: Liselott 'Lottie' Tham (née Persson, born 1949) is the daughter of H&M founder Erling Persson and sister of longtime H&M chairman Stefan Persson. Her wealth comes from her inherited H&M shareholding of roughly 5%, which makes her the fashion retailer's second-largest shareholder after her brother. She lives in Stockholm and keeps a very low public profile.
interesting_fact: She holds about 5.3% of H&M, making her the retailer's second-largest shareholder, behind only her brother Stefan Persson (about 37.7%).
notes: Goes by 'Lottie Tham'. Extremely private, no public channels or interviews found; H&M media relations is corporate, not her personal office. Married to financier Pieter Tham. Fit for an energy/data-center podcast is weak.

name: Bajrang Lal Kheruka
current_role: Deceased (died 12 December 2021); was Chairman Emeritus of Borosil
notes: B.L. Kheruka (born 1930) died on 12 Dec 2021 per Glass Worldwide tribute: https://www.glassworldwide.co.uk/industry-announcements/remembering-mr-b-l-kheruka . He acquired Corning's Borosil stake in 1988. Family business now led by son Pradeep Kheruka (Chairman) and grandson Shreevar Kheruka (MD & CEO, Borosil Ltd); Borosil Renewables (solar glass) may interest an energy podcast.

name: Laurence Escalante
current_role: Founder and former CEO/executive chairman of VGW (Virtual Gaming Worlds); resigned July 2026, now focused on private businesses (Lance East)
profile: Perth entrepreneur who founded VGW in 2010, building sweepstakes-style social casino brands Chumba Casino, LuckyLand Slots and Global Poker aimed mainly at US players; VGW reported close to $4bn revenue in 2024. In 2025 he took the company fully private by buying out minority holders. He resigned as CEO and chairman in July 2026 and has since moved into ventures such as luxury car dealer Lance East Exotics.
interesting_fact: VGW started in 2010 in Escalante's basement in Perth and grew into a business with close to $4bn annual revenue, almost all from the US market.
notes: CAUTION: he stepped down as VGW CEO in Jan 2026 after being charged in Perth (alleged assault and drug offences, which he denies) and resigned permanently on 3 July 2026 (https://sbcamericas.com/2026/07/06/vgw-founder-escalante-resigns-as-ceo/). Also faces a ~$60m contract claim. No published personal contact found; VGW press office no longer represents him. Likely not a suitable guest at present.

name: Craig Newmark
current_role: Founder, Craigslist; founder of Craig Newmark Philanthropies
profile: Craig Newmark spent ~17 years at IBM and then worked at Charles Schwab in San Francisco, where in 1995 he started an email list of local events that became Craigslist. Now largely focused on philanthropy through Craig Newmark Philanthropies (founded 2015), funding trustworthy journalism, cybersecurity ('cyber civil defense'), veterans and military families, and women in tech; he joined the Giving Pledge in Dec 2025.
interesting_fact: Craigslist started out as an email newsletter about events in San Francisco; Newmark launched it from his flat while working as a Schwab systems/security consultant.
deep_cut_fact: He is a devoted bird lover (since the mid-80s in Detroit) and a champion of pigeons, which he calls 'the underdog... possibly our successor species'; he has been a top funder of SF pigeon rescue Palomacy since 2013.
notes: Very accessible and media-friendly, active on social media (also craignewmark@mastodon.social). Journalism-funding focus makes him a natural podcast guest; cybersecurity/infrastructure angle is a hook.

name: Rihanna
current_role: Singer; founder of Fenty Beauty (co-owned with LVMH) and co-owner of Savage X Fenty; founder of the Clara Lionel Foundation
profile: Robyn Rihanna Fenty, from Barbados (country field in input is wrong), became a global pop star after being discovered by Jay-Z as a teenager. name: Richard Yuengling Jr
current_role: Owner and CEO, D.G. Yuengling & Son (America's oldest brewery), Pottsville, Pennsylvania
profile: Dick Yuengling, fifth-generation owner of D.G. Yuengling & Son, bought out his father in 1985 and turned a struggling 137,000-barrel regional brewery into one of America's largest brewers (~2m barrels a year), largely on Yuengling Lager. His four daughters work in the business and are being primed to succeed him; in 2026 the brand is expanding into Wisconsin and Iowa.
interesting_fact: Yuengling, opened in Pottsville in 1829, survived Prohibition by making ice cream and near beer.
deep_cut_fact: He knew by age 10 he wanted to run the brewery and started working there part-time around 15; he admits that when Yuengling isn't on tap, he'll order a Sam Adams or Sierra Nevada. His brewing philosophy: 'We stay nuts and bolts — we make beer.'
notes: Down-to-earth, avoids publicity. Press contact is brewery media relations (Bethany Ingerick) per 2026 releases. Daughter Wendy Yuengling (Chief Administrative Officer) is the more public family spokesperson.

name: Stefanie Westphal Thompson
profile: Daughter of Vertex founders Ray and Antoinette Westphal, she joined the Pennsylvania tax-software company in 1991 (roles incl. Treasurer) and has been a director since the early 1990s. With siblings Jeffrey Westphal and Amanda Westphal Radcliffe she bought the firm from their parents in 2000 and took it public in July 2020; Vertex now generates over $800m in annual revenue.
interesting_fact: Vertex, started by her parents in 1978, was bought by the three Westphal siblings in 2000 and listed in 2020, making both sisters billionaires.
deep_cut_fact: An engineer by training: she holds dual BAs in Engineering and Economics from Lafayette College plus a Fordham finance MBA, and before Vertex was a Chemical Bank VP covering middle-market companies; she has also been vice-chair of the Bryn Mawr Hospital Foundation board.
notes: Low public profile; no personal social accounts found. Corporate contacts route to Vertex comms/IR (CEO is Christopher Young).

name: Luca Barilla
profile: Born in Milan in 1960, Luca Barilla is one of three brothers (with Guido and Paolo) who with their family own about 85% of Barilla, the Parma-based pasta and bakery group whose brands include Barilla, Mulino Bianco and Wasa. He joined the family business in 1980, trained at Barilla France and in the US, and has been deputy chairman since 1988; he also invests in confectionery.
interesting_fact: In 2018 he and his wife Michela Petronio bought Pastiglie Leone, the historic Turin maker of pastilles and sweets, after earlier running confectioner GranMilano as president from 1997 until its sale in 2008.
deep_cut_fact: Before rising in the family firm he studied in the United States and did his military service with Italy's Carabinieri; he started at Barilla in 1980 and became a product manager in 1984.
notes: Low media profile compared with brother Guido (chairman). Barilla's media relations office is the realistic route. Pastiglie Leone ownership offers a personal angle.

name: Rosa Brescia Cafferata
current_role: Director of Grupo Breca entities (e.g. Minsur, Breca Banca); President of CPAL (Peruvian Center for Hearing, Language and Learning)
profile: Peruvian heiress (born c. 1926), daughter of Italian-born Fortunato Brescia Tassano and María Catalina Cafferata, whose surnames gave Grupo Breca its name. Breca spans mining (Minsur), banking, fishing (TASA), cement, real estate and more; she and her children hold about 30% of it. Her son Alex Fort Brescia co-chairs the group.
interesting_fact: The conglomerate's name 'Breca' is formed from her parents' surnames, BREscia and CAfferata.
notes: Would be about 100 years old; no death report found but not confirmed alive. Extremely private. Realistic podcast contact is the group's co-chairmen (Alex Fort Brescia, Pedro Brescia Moreyra) via Breca corporate communications; Minsur (tin/mining) gives an energy-transition angle.
